subject: Throughput & commit phasing — proposed SLA remedy language for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbushealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on Dedicated commit phasing and SLA remedies

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the call last week. Our procurement/legal team asked for a few clarifications before we proceed to a PO: specifically around how Redwood defines the committed unit for Dedicated, how throughput guarantees are measured during a phased ramp, and what the ladder of service credits looks like if we miss targets. A couple concrete asks: 

- Exact operational definition of the billing unit (we saw references to "capacity units" in the term sheet; want to ensure we align on math).
- If we sign a 12-month commit with a 3-month ramp (e.g., month 1 = 40% of commit, month 2 = 70%, month 3 = 100%), how are throughput guarantees prorated and how are credits applied if throughput misses during ramp months?
- Any clauses for unused committed capacity (conversion to credits, carry-forward, or refunds).

Attaching the procurement checklist — we can also have our legal send redlines if helpful.

Appreciate the quick guidance here so we can move to commercial terms.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Cloud Procurement
Nimbus Health
Attachment: procurement_checklist.pdf (PDF)

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated commit phasing and SLA remedies

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are our proposed definitions and a pragmatic approach for ramp months; I attached a working redline of our SLA (draft_SLA_redline_v1.pdf). High level: we aim to make math explicit so procurement can map commits to expected throughput and cost.

Key definitions (proposed):
- "GPU Slot-Hour (GSH)": the billing unit equals one GPU slot reserved for one hour of wall-clock time on Redwood Dedicated. A GSH maps to a fixed compute envelope (GPU type, baseline memory, and baseline NVLink config), and is the atomic reserved unit customers commit to.
- "Throughput Guarantee": the platform guarantees median token throughput per GSH for the plan-class/model family at a defined latency percentile. Example: for T4-class equivalent, baseline = 45 tokens/sec per GSH at p50 for warm in-GPU cache requests (numbers in redline table).

Phasing / ramp rules: 
- Commit month targets are expressed in GSH/month. During ramp months, the guaranteed throughput is pro-rated to the committed GSH allocated for that month.
- Measurement windows: we evaluate SLO compliance on a rolling 30-day window by default, but will apply a 14-day window to the final ramp month if Nimbus requires faster stabilization reporting — we can set that in the contract.
- Credits during ramp: service credits are computed against the monthly invoice for that month using the remedy ladder; however, for months designated as "ramp", credits are scaled by the ramp percentage (e.g., month 1 at 40% commitment -> credit exposure limited to 40% of remedy value). This avoids full-credit exposure during predictable onboarding ramp.

Unused committed GSH: 
- Standard: unused committed GSH cannot be refunded but may be converted to platform credits at 70% of invoice value if requested quarterly. 
- Alternate: for 24-month contracts we can offer a 90% conversion rate for the unused portion (to be captured in the commercial schedule).

Remedy ladder (illustrative — full table in redline):
- p95 latency breach >5% of measurement window -> 5% credit of monthly Dedicated invoice.
- p95 latency breach >15% -> 10% credit.
- p95 latency breach >30% or sustained degradation (more than one consecutive window) -> 20% credit + escalation path.

I attached draft_SLA_redline_v1.pdf with the above language and placeholders for numbers we should finalize with you. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft_SLA_redline_v1.pdf (PDF)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Nimbus pricing posture & redline asks

Sean/Ben —

Looping in our commercial posture for Nimbus. A few negotiation items to add to the redline before we send back to Daniel:

- Pricing tiers: propose list price per GSH = $0.95/hr. Volume discounts at commit thresholds: 12-month commit >= 1,000 GSH/month -> 10% off list; >= 5,000 -> 18%; >= 10,000 -> 25%. These thresholds are flexible in discussion but give us a starting point.
- Ramp flexibility: allow a one-time 30% ramp delay in months 1–3 without penalty (i.e., if Nimbus hits month 4 full commit, earlier months' shortfall won't accrue service-credit debt). This is important for large integrations.
- Unused conversion: I prefer convert-to-credit option but set conversion to 70% as Sean suggested. Also add a clause for 6-month lookback reporting so they can request conversion only once per quarter.
- Remedy cap: cap service credits at 50% of the monthly Dedicated invoice for that month. Legal will push back if uncapped.

I'm attaching the updated pricing model I used to show the margin impact (pricing_model_v2.xlsx). Once Ben confirms, we should include an explicit alternate commercial schedule for a 24-month deal with a steeper discount and higher conversion rate.

-LB
Lauren Bishop
VP, Commercials
Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (XLSX)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: Nimbus pricing posture & redline asks

Agree with Lauren. A few practical items we should pre-clear with Nimbus before sending redlines to avoid time-consuming back-and-forth:

- Ask for expected model mix and 95th/median sequence lengths; throughput guarantees are model-sensitive and we should align on the two or three model families they plan to serve.
- Offer a first-year commercial incentive: 10% off list for the first 12 months on a 12-month commit (or 15% if they sign 24 months). Also include a one-time onboarding credit equal to 50 GSH to help offset migration testing.
- On the remedy cap: propose legal-friendly language: "Service credits shall not exceed the lesser of (a) 50% of the monthly Dedicated invoice for the period, or (b) the aggregate fees paid for the trailing 30 days." This gives them protections while bounding our exposure.

Quote to add to redline (suggested wording):

> "If Redwood fails to meet the Throughput Guarantee for any measurement window, Customer may be eligible for Service Credits as set out in the Remedy Ladder. Service Credits are calculated as a percentage of the Monthly Dedicated Invoice for the applicable measurement window, and shall not exceed 50% of that invoice."

I'll greenlight sending the redline to Daniel once Sean confirms the conversion terms and the ramp-safe harbor language.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on Dedicated commit phasing and SLA remedies — next steps

Daniel —

Thanks for the note and patience while we pulled internal comments together. Summary and next steps below so procurement/legal have a clean package to review: 

Summary of what we propose to include in the commercial schedule/redline: 
- Billing unit: GPU Slot-Hour (GSH) as defined in the attached redline.
- Ramp: pro-rated throughput guarantees during ramp months; measurement default = rolling 30-day window, optional 14-day stabilization window for the final ramp month upon request.
- Credits during ramp scaled by ramp percentage; one-time ramp-safe harbor (30% flexibility) built into months 1–3.
- Unused committed GSH: conversion to platform credits at 70% invoice value (90% if 24-month commit). Requests for conversion allowed quarterly with a 6-month lookback.
- Remedy ladder: tiered credits (5/10/20%) with a cap at 50% of the monthly Dedicated invoice. Proposed legal-friendly cap language included.
- Commercial incentives: 10% off list first year for 12-month commit (15% for 24 months) + one-time onboarding credit (50 GSH) — pending your confirmation of model mix / usage profile.

Next steps: 
1) We will share a cleaned redline (draft_SLA_redline_v2.pdf) with the items above incorporated.
2) If Nimbus is OK with the high-level approach, let's schedule a 30-minute legal/commercial sync on Wednesday to walk the redline and confirm conversion/discount numbers.
3) Please share expected model families and 95th/median sequence lengths before the call so we can lock throughput numbers.

If that all sounds good, I'll send the updated redline and book time. Appreciate you moving quickly on this.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft_SLA_redline_v1.pdf (PDF)
